subject: Data processing role, telemetry mapping, and evidence pack request
messages:
From: Sonia Patel <privacy@venturehealth.com>
To: aditya_rao <aditya_rao@redwood.ai>
Cc: Tom Reed <legal@venturehealth.com>
Date: Mon, 20 Jul 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Data processing role & telemetry mapping for CCPA/CPRA

Hi Aditya,

Thanks for taking this on. VentureHealth is preparing a short privacy addendum for our US customers (CCPA/CPRA obligations) and we need a concise evidence pack from Redwood to close internal risk review. Specifically we need:

- Confirmation of role: that Redwood will act solely as a service provider/processor (no sale of personal data).
- A current list of subprocessors, with locations and function (or the cadence by which you notify customers of additions).
- A mapping of telemetry/telemetry categories you collect by default (logs, error traces, aggregated usage, sample payloads) and retention periods.
- Interstate transfer safeguards and whether you rely on any cross-jurisdiction transfers for telemetry or backups.
- SOC 2 / security attestations and where we can download them.

We attached a short questionnaire (VentureHealth-Questionnaire.xlsx) — answers to the highlighted rows would be most helpful. Can your team deliver an initial pack by EOB tomorrow PST? If not, please propose timing.

Sonia Patel
Director, Privacy & Data Governance
VentureHealth
privacy@venturehealth.com

Attachment: VentureHealth-Questionnaire.xlsx (xlsx)

From: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.ai>
To: Sonia Patel <privacy@venturehealth.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 20 Jul 2026 11:03:12 -0700
Subject: Re: Data processing role & telemetry mapping for CCPA/CPRA

Sonia — thanks for the clear list. Short answers up front: Redwood operates as a service provider/processor, we do not sell personal data, and we can provide the subprocessors list + telemetry mapping.

I'll outline next steps below and attach a short DPA summary and our standard evidence pointers. We'll prioritize the items you flagged and propose a two-step delivery: initial evidence pack (subprocessors + telemetry mapping + SOC2 link) within 48 hours, followed by a finalized DPA addendum and DocuSign routing within 5 business days.

What we'll deliver in the initial pack:
- CSV of current subprocessors (roles, regions, contact)
- Telemetry mapping PDF (event categories, default retention, sample anonymized records)
- SOC 2 Type II public link and attestations summary
- Short note on cross-jurisdiction backups/replication and contractual safeguards

Questions for you (so we tailor the mapping):
1) Do you require per-endpoint retention overrides, or is a company-level retention window okay for your use case?
2) Are you expecting telemetry samples that include prompt/response content, or only metadata/latency traces?

I'll attach the initial summary (Redwood-US-DPA-summary.pdf). Ben and Neha are looped for subprocessor and telemetry detail.

Best,
Aditya Rao
Head of Legal Ops (acting) — Redwood Inference
aditya_rao@redwood.ai

Attachment: Redwood-US-DPA-summary.pdf (pdf)

Date: Tue, 21 Jul 2026 08:15:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Data processing role & telemetry mapping for CCPA/CPRA

Hi Sonia — following up on Aditya's note with the telemetry and subprocessor details you asked for. Key points:

- Telemetry categories (high level): request metadata (timestamp, client IP obfuscated), request/response size, model/endpoint id, latency, error codes, aggregated usage counters.
- Content retention: by default we store full request/response artifacts for 30 days for debugging; customers can opt into longer retention for observability or disable content retention entirely.
- Anonymization: we redact deterministic PII fields from telemetry exports unless the customer has explicitly configured content retention.
- Cross-jurisdiction backups: primary replication is within region; for DR we replicate to a paired region (US-west <-> US-east). We rely on contractual safeguards and standard encryption-in-transit + at-rest. No transfer outside the US for US-region accounts unless explicitly configured.

Attached: a current subprocessor export (redwood-subprocessors-20260722.csv) and a telemetry mapping PDF. If you need a CSV with location-by-function grouped differently, say which column format you prefer and we'll re-export.

Ben Carter
Senior Sales Engineer, Redwood Inference
ben_carter@redwood.ai

Attachments: redwood-subprocessors-20260722.csv (csv), redwood-telemetry-mapping-2026-07-22.pdf (pdf)

From: Sonia Patel <privacy@venturehealth.com>
To: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
Cc: Tom Reed <legal@venturehealth.com>
Date: Tue, 21 Jul 2026 14:22:36 -0700
Subject: Re: Data processing role & telemetry mapping for CCPA/CPRA

Thanks Ben — that helps. A couple follow-ups from legal:

- Retention: VentureHealth needs assurance that default 30-day content retention can be limited to metadata-only for our production workload (we can't permit content retention without explicit consent). Can Redwood scope that to a per-account config?
- Subprocessors: please confirm the notification cadence for new subprocessors (we prefer 30-day advance notice for anything that processes personal data). Can Redwood provide an API or subscription to automated notices?
- Transfers: your note about paired-region replication is helpful. For our legal, can you provide the specific contractual language Redwood proposes for interstate transfers and backups (we prefer a clause that prohibits transfer outside the US without written consent)?

I've attached a draft of the VentureHealth addendum (VH-Privacy-Addendum-Draft.docx) with redlines where necessary. If you can populate the clauses we discussed and return a clean DPA addendum, we can route internally for sign-off.

Sonia

Attachment: VH-Privacy-Addendum-Draft.docx (docx)

From: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.ai>
To: Sonia Patel <privacy@venturehealth.com>, Tom Reed <legal@venturehealth.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 22 Jul 2026 16:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Data processing role & telemetry mapping for CCPA/CPRA

Sonia / Tom — thanks for the redlines and the clear asks. Summary of commitments and next steps below (MIAP style):

1) Role and sale of data: Redwood confirms in writing that we operate as a service provider/processor and do not sell personal data. We'll include the clause verbatim in the addendum.

2) Subprocessors: we will provide a real-time export and a notification subscription. Action: output CSV and a webhook/API that notifies customers of additions. Timing: we will provide the initial full list attached (redwood-subprocessors-20260722.csv) today and enable subscription within 3 business days.

3) Retention controls: we can scope content retention on a per-account basis. By default it's 30 days; we will add a per-account toggle to set content retention to metadata-only (no content stored) within the standard account settings. Action & timing: enable toggle and documentation within 5 business days; implementation roadmap attached to the addendum.

4) Transfers & backups: Redwood will include a clause that prohibits transfer outside the US for US-region accounts without written consent. For DR replication within the US we will document paired-region behavior and encryption safeguards in the addendum.

5) Evidence: SOC 2 Type II report link and attestations are available here: https://docs.redwood.ai/dpa/US-DPA-Redwood-2026.pdf. We'll also provide redacted telemetry samples and mapping in the Drive link: https://drive.google.com/redwood/telemetry-mapping-2026.

6) DPA routing: We'll prepare a clean addendum with the agreed language and send a DocuSign link (https://app.docusign.com/documents/ABC12345). Expect the draft by EOD tomorrow; DocuSign to follow once we align.

If this aligns with VentureHealth's needs, we'll proceed and I will have Neha confirm the exact toggle behavior and Ben validate the export formats.

Best regards,
Aditya Rao
Head of Legal Ops (acting) — Redwood Inference
aditya_rao@redwood.ai
